Function purpose: Evaluate this visual decision node within the full program; diagnose semantic disagreement or insufficient robustness without forcing answers.

<INPUTS_TO_FUNCTION> **Node(role: one immutable-snapshot executable visual decision node to repair semantically)**: {"active_on": ["pass", "fail", "unknown"], "binding": "Assess only visible changes in (...) pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?", "role": "support"} </INPUTS_TO_FUNCTION>

<OUTPUT_OF_FUNCTION> {"reference_label": "partial", "aggregate": {"agreement": 0.0, "coverage": 1.0, "label_distribution": {"yes": 1}}, "node_traces": [{"check_id": "s2", "status": "pass", "evidence": "The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines, indicating progress toward the requested style.", "valid": true, "eligible": true, "queried": true, "confidence": 0.98, "completion_tokens": 61, "dependencies": [], "execution_ref": "61a9e73a7533f4b359d46fbc72f7b59e93cb8c4c13b3d7aa85392bca84d0ede3", "failure": null}], "downstream_gradients": {"fulfillment": ["The node\u2019s binding asks whether the image appears as a *completed* pencil drawing, but its criteria make s1 passing sufficient for \u201cyes.\u201d That lets evidence of a muted, grainy pencil-like treatment override the distinction between visible progress and completion; s2\u2019s wording (\u201cindicating progress\u201d) also does not establish completion. Tighten the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is substantially realized across the image, while partial requires supported visible progress that falls short, and absent requires supported lack of progress. Apply those thresholds to the actual source/edit comparison: the edit visibly changes the meal and setting into a pale, grainy, sketch-like rendering, but the traces do not explain why that amounts to a completed drawing rather than partial progress. Require the supports to distinguish those states explicitly and ground their judgments in visual evidence, rather than treating two correlated \u201cpass\u201d labels as independent proof. Preserve unknown when evidence cannot resolve the distinction. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here; the mismatch is semantic calibration and criterion ambiguity."]}} </OUTPUT_OF_FUNCTION>

payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines, indicating progress toward the requested style.

fulfillment: The node’s binding asks whether the image appears as a *completed* pencil drawing, but its criteria make s1 passing sufficient for “yes.” That lets evidence of a muted, grainy pencil-like treatment override the distinction between visible progress and completion; s2’s wording (“indicating progress”) also does not establish completion. Tighten the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is substantially realized across the image, while partial requires supported visible progress that falls short, and absent requires supported lack of progress. Apply those thresholds to the actual source/edit comparison: the edit visibly changes the meal and setting into a pale, grainy, sketch-like rendering, but the traces do not explain why that amounts to a completed drawing rather than partial progress. Require the supports to distinguish those states explicitly and ground their judgments in visual evidence, rather than treating two correlated “pass” labels as independent proof. Preserve unknown when evidence cannot resolve the distinction. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here; the mismatch is semantic calibration and criterion ambiguity.

response.content: {"text":"The node correctly detects visible progress, but its progress-only question cannot distinguish the rubric’s three outcomes; a pass is being treated downstream as completed “yes.” Keep this support node narrowly about image-grounded progress, and make its typed criteria explicitly report evidence for progress versus no progress, reserving unknown for insufficient visual evidence. Ensure the parent decision separately assesses whether the transformation is substantially complete before assigning yes, and partial when visible progress falls short. Ground the comparison in the source and edit: the edit retains the scene while applying a pale, muted, grainy, sketch-like treatment across the meal and surroundings. That supports progress, but the trace should not imply that progress alone establishes completion. Do not count correlated pass labels as independent evidence. This is semantic criterion/routing ambiguity, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
